exercises.title: Your First InDesign Document
exercises.task: Create a document, choose a page size, set margins, add pages, save the file, navigate it, and export a PDF.
requirements: Custom page size (not the default preset)
instructions: Create a new document with a page size of your choice.
Set margins to something other than the default.
Add a second page via the Pages panel.
Save the file.
Export a PDF and open it to confirm it looks right.
hints: File > New > Document is where page size and margins live.
The '+' icon at the bottom of the Pages panel adds pages.
commonMistakes: Forgetting to save before exporting
Not noticing the page size shown in the title bar doesn't match what you intended
selfAssessment: Did the document open with the size and margins I set?
Does the exported PDF match what I see on screen?

exercises.title: Three Frames, No Overlap
exercises.task: Create a text frame, an image frame, and a plain shape on one page, arranged without overlapping.
requirements: One text frame with real content
instructions: Use the Rectangle Frame tool for the image frame.
Use the Type tool for the text frame.
Use the Rectangle tool for the shape.
Align all three using Object > Align.
hints: Press F for frame tool, T for type tool, R for rectangle.
Shift-click to select multiple objects before aligning.
commonMistakes: Accidentally nesting one frame inside another
Using the wrong tool and getting a shape when you wanted a text frame
selfAssessment: Can I tell each frame type apart at a glance?
Are the frames aligned to a consistent edge?

exercises.title: Format a Raw Paragraph
exercises.task: Take an unformatted block of placeholder text and turn it into a readable, styled paragraph with a heading.
requirements: A clear heading, larger and bolder than body text
First-line indent on body paragraphs after the first
instructions: Paste in several paragraphs of placeholder text.
Format a heading at the top.
Set leading and alignment for the body text.
Apply a first-line indent using the Paragraph panel, not spaces.
hints: Use Ctrl/Cmd+A to select all text before applying body-wide settings.
First-line indent is a specific Paragraph panel field, not a tab character.
commonMistakes: Using spacebar/tab for indents instead of the real setting
Justifying a narrow column and getting ugly spacing
selfAssessment: Is the heading clearly distinguishable from body text?
Does the paragraph read comfortably at arm's length?

exercises.title: Three Frames, One Photo
exercises.task: Place the same image into a square, a tall, and a wide frame, and fit each proportionally without distortion.
requirements: Same source image in all 3 frames
No stretching or distortion in any frame
Each crop shows the subject sensibly
instructions: Draw 3 frames of different proportions.
Place the same image into each.
Apply Fill Frame Proportionally to each.
Reposition the image within each frame using the Direct Selection tool if needed.
hints: Object > Fitting has every fitting option.
Direct Selection (A) lets you drag the image inside its frame.
commonMistakes: Using Fit Content to Frame, which stretches the image
Not checking that the subject is still visible after cropping
selfAssessment: Does the image look natural, not stretched, in all three frames?
Is the subject still recognizable in the tightest crop?

exercises.title: Typography Challenge: Fix This Paragraph
exercises.task: You're given a badly set paragraph: single font, no hierarchy, tight leading, fully justified in a narrow column. Improve hierarchy, spacing, alignment, and overall readability.
requirements: Add at least one level of visual hierarchy
Fix leading to a comfortable reading value
Reconsider alignment given the column width
Fix any obviously loose or tight kerning on headline-sized text
instructions: Identify what's wrong before changing anything — write down 3 issues.
Fix leading first.
Reconsider justification vs. left alignment for the column width.
Add a simple heading with real hierarchy if one is missing.
hints: Narrow columns usually read better left-aligned than justified.
120% of font size is a solid leading starting point.
commonMistakes: Changing five things at once without checking each improvement individually
Over-correcting leading to be too loose
selfAssessment: Would a stranger find this easier to read than the original?
Is there a clear point of entry (a heading or lead-in) to the paragraph?

exercises.title: 3-Column Grid Poster
exercises.task: Design an A4 poster using a strict 3-column grid: headline, subtitle, body, contact info, 1 image, 3mm bleed, max 2 fonts.
requirements: Headline, subtitle, body, contact info all present
instructions: Set up the document with a 3-column grid via Layout > Margins and Columns.
Block in your headline spanning all 3 columns.
Place the image spanning 1–2 columns.
Fit body text and contact info into the remaining space.
Check every element aligns to a column guide.
hints: Turn on View > Grids & Guides > Show Guides while working.
Snap to Guides (View > Grids & Guides) makes alignment automatic.
commonMistakes: Setting up the grid, then eyeballing placement anyway
Using more than 2 fonts out of habit
selfAssessment: Does every element align to at least one grid line?
Is there a single clear focal point?

exercises.title: Build a Repeating Footer System
exercises.task: Build an 8-page document where every page automatically shows a footer with the document title and an automatic page number.
requirements: A parent page with a footer text frame
Automatic page number marker (not typed manually)
At least one intentional override on one page
instructions: Edit the parent page and build the footer.
Insert the automatic page number marker.
Apply the parent to all document pages.
Override the footer on one page intentionally (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+click) and change its color there only.
hints: Type > Insert Special Character > Markers > Current Page Number.
Overrides need Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+click on the object to break the link to the parent.
commonMistakes: Typing page numbers manually instead of using the marker
Editing a document page directly when meaning to edit the parent
selfAssessment: Do page numbers update correctly across all 8 pages?
Can I explain the difference between the parent and an override?

exercises.title: Format 20 Paragraphs, 3 Styles Only
exercises.task: Format a document of 20 mixed headings and paragraphs using no more than 3 paragraph styles, applied consistently, with zero manual (local) overrides.
requirements: Updating one style visibly cascades to every instance
instructions: Create Heading, Subheading, and Body paragraph styles from your best-formatted examples.
Apply each style to the matching paragraphs throughout the document.
Resist the urge to manually tweak anything — fix the style instead.
Test: change the Body style's leading and confirm all body paragraphs update.
hints: The Paragraph Styles panel shows a '+' next to a style name if local overrides exist.
Clear Overrides (Alt/Option-click the style) removes stray manual formatting.
commonMistakes: Creating a 4th or 5th style out of convenience instead of solving the problem within 3
Leaving local overrides that make future updates unpredictable
selfAssessment: Does the Paragraph Styles panel show zero '+' override indicators?
Did changing one style update every paragraph using it?

exercises.title: Zero Overset Across 3 Pages
exercises.task: Take a long article and thread it across 3 pages with zero overset text remaining.
requirements: Text flows across exactly 3 threaded frames
Text threads visible and logical in reading order
instructions: Paste a long article into a single frame so it overflows.
Click the red '+' and thread into a second frame on page 2.
Repeat for a third frame on page 3.
Turn on View > Extras > Show Text Threads to visually confirm the order.
hints: The out-port is the small square in a frame's bottom-right corner.
Show Text Threads only displays when the connected frames are selected.
commonMistakes: Threading frames out of reading order
Shrinking font size to avoid threading instead of doing it properly
selfAssessment: Is there any red '+' remaining anywhere in the document?
Does the text read in the correct order across all 3 frames?

exercises.title: Styled Price Table
exercises.task: Build a 4-column, 8-row price table with a distinct header row and alternating row colors.
requirements: Saved as a reusable Table Style
instructions: Insert a table into a text frame with Table > Insert Table.
Fill in header labels and sample data.
Style the header row with bold text and a fill color.
Apply Table > Table Options > Alternating Fills.
Save the formatting as a new Table Style.
hints: Select the whole header row before applying fill/bold, not cell by cell.
Table Styles are saved from the Table Styles panel's 'New Style' option.
commonMistakes: Manually formatting each row instead of using Alternating Fills
Forgetting to save the formatting as a reusable style
selfAssessment: Is the header instantly distinguishable from data rows?
Could I apply this exact style to a brand-new table in one click?

exercises.title: Zero-Error Preflight
exercises.task: Take a deliberately broken file (missing link, overset text, low-res image) and fix every issue until Preflight shows a green dot.
instructions: Open Window > Output > Preflight and review every listed error.
Click each error to jump directly to the problem.
Fix links, resize/replace low-res images, and resolve overset text.
Confirm the Preflight indicator turns green.
hints: Missing links can be fixed via the Links panel's 'Relink' button.
Low effective PPI usually means the image was scaled up too much — shrink the frame or replace the image.
commonMistakes: Fixing the visible errors but missing one hidden on another page
Ignoring a warning because 'it looks fine on screen'
selfAssessment: Does the Preflight panel show a green dot with zero errors?
Would this file be safe to send to a commercial printer?

diagnostics.title: What's Wrong With This Business Card?
diagnostics.issue: Text runs almost to the very edge of the card with no visible safe margin, and the background color stops short of the trim edge on two sides.
diagnostics.reveal: The text has no safe margin (risking being trimmed off) and the background isn't extended into the bleed, which will leave a thin white sliver after cutting. Fix: pull text in from the trim edge by at least 3–5mm, and extend the background fully into the bleed area.

diagnostics.title: What's Wrong With This Paragraph?
diagnostics.issue: A dense block of fully justified text in a narrow single column, tight leading, no paragraph spacing, and no heading.
diagnostics.reveal: Justification in a narrow column causes uneven word spacing; tight leading with no paragraph breaks makes it exhausting to read; and there's no entry point (heading) to orient the reader. Fix: switch to left alignment, loosen leading to ~120% of font size, and add a clear heading.

diagnostics.title: What's Wrong With This Poster?
diagnostics.issue: Three different focal points compete for attention — a large headline, an equally large image, and a bright colored shape — none clearly dominant.
diagnostics.reveal: Without one dominant element, the eye doesn't know where to look first. Fix: choose one hero element (usually the headline or the image, not both) and reduce the size or contrast of the other elements so they support rather than compete.

diagnostics.title: What's Wrong With This Table?
diagnostics.issue: Every row looks identical — same weight, same color, no visual separation between the header and data.
diagnostics.reveal: Without contrast between header and data rows, the table is hard to scan quickly. Fix: bold and/or fill the header row distinctly, and consider alternating fills on data rows to help the eye track across.

diagnostics.title: What's Wrong With This Print File?
diagnostics.issue: The Preflight panel shows a red dot with 4 warnings, but the file was exported anyway.
diagnostics.reveal: Ignoring Preflight warnings risks sending a broken file to print — missing fonts substitute silently, low-res images print blurry, and overset text simply disappears. Fix: resolve every Preflight warning before export, every time.

diagnostics.title: What's Wrong With This Flyer's Type?
diagnostics.issue: The headline, subtitle, and body text are all the same size and weight, differentiated only by slightly different fonts.
diagnostics.reveal: Without size or weight contrast, there's no real hierarchy — the reader has to work to figure out what matters most. Fix: build hierarchy through deliberate size and weight contrast, not font-swapping alone.

recreate.title: Recreate: Minimalist Event Poster
recreate.reference: A large centered headline in a bold sans-serif, a thin horizontal rule beneath it, and small centered date/location text below that. Generous white margin on all sides.
hints: Center alignment plus generous whitespace does most of the work here.
The rule is a simple stroked line, not a frame border.
evaluationChecklist: Headline is the clear focal point
Rule is thin and precisely centered
Overall composition matches the reference's balance

recreate.title: Recreate: Editorial Two-Column Article
recreate.reference: A magazine-style spread: a large pull-quote breaking across two columns, a drop cap on the opening paragraph, and an image with tight text wrap in the lower column.
hints: Drop caps are set in the Paragraph panel's Drops and Nested Styles section.
The pull-quote is a separate text frame layered over the columns, not part of the threaded story.
evaluationChecklist: Two columns are evenly threaded with no overset
Drop cap is applied correctly, not manually resized text
Pull-quote reads as a distinct visual break
Image text wrap looks intentional, not accidental

recreate.title: Recreate: Grid-Based Price List
recreate.reference: A restaurant-style price list: section headers in a heavier weight, item names left-aligned, prices right-aligned with a dotted leader connecting them.
hints: Dotted leaders are configured in the Tabs panel (Type > Tabs), not typed manually as periods.
Consistent spacing between items matters as much as the alignment itself.
evaluationChecklist: All prices align in a single vertical line
Leader dots are evenly spaced, not manually typed
Section headers are visually distinct from items

recreate.title: Recreate: Cover Page With Registration Marks Motif
recreate.reference: A bold cover treatment using crop-mark-style corner ticks as a graphic device framing the title, echoing real print registration marks.
hints: Small precise line segments at each corner, grouped, recreate the crop-mark motif.
Keep the title's baseline aligned to where real crop marks would sit for authenticity.
evaluationChecklist: Corner ticks are consistent in length and weight
Title placement relates logically to the tick marks
Overall composition feels intentional, not decorative for its own sake

5min: Fix the kerning on a single headline word.
Change one paragraph from justified to left-aligned and compare readability.
Apply a fitting option to a stretched image.
Insert an automatic page number marker into a text frame.
Create one new paragraph style from existing formatted text.
15min: Build a 3-column grid and place 3 text blocks aligned to it.
Thread a long paragraph across two frames with zero overset.
Create a simple 4x4 table with a styled header row.
Fix a badly kerned, badly leaded headline-and-subhead pair.
Set up bleed on an existing document and extend one background element into it.
30min: Design a business card from a one-line client brief you invent yourself.
Build a parent page with footer, page number, and running header, then apply it to 5 pages.
Take a wall of unformatted text and turn it into a styled article with 3 paragraph styles.
Recreate a poster layout from a reference image using only type and a rule line.
Preflight and export a print-ready PDF from an existing project file.
